title: Global Soil Organic Carbon Map (GSOCmap)
claim: Monitoring and mapping soil organic carbon, as FAO's Global Soil Organic Carbon Map does at national and global scale, provides the baseline data needed to identify degraded soils and set realistic targets for rebuilding lost carbon stocks through land management change.
evidence_text: FAO's Global Soil Organic Carbon Map (GSOCmap) was produced through a consultative process involving FAO member countries to establish a global baseline of soil organic carbon distribution. The map is intended to help land managers and policymakers identify degraded areas, set soil organic carbon restoration targets, and evaluate the sequestration potential of land management practices that rebuild organic matter, such as reduced tillage and residue retention, over time.
